findings.title: High-impact residual risk accepted outside delegated authority
findings.condition: S-01 residual risk acceptance RA-01 was signed by the project manager rather than the VP Engineering required by the approved delegation.
findings.criteria: Residual risks are documented and accepted by an official with the authority set for that level of risk, with conditions and an expiry.
findings.cause: The acceptance workflow did not check the signer against the authority matrix.
findings.effect: A material residual risk remains without valid acceptance by the accountable authority.
findings.recommendation: Obtain a new VP Engineering decision with explicit conditions and expiry; add delegated-authority validation to the acceptance workflow and independently retest T5.
findings.severityWhy: A mandatory high-impact risk acceptance control failed. Current independent human scheduling limits immediate exposure but does not cure the approval deficiency.
findings.safeguards: Keep AI priorities advisory; require independent human scheduling authorization until the proper authority makes and records a decision.
findings.dependencies: None beyond the named decision and responsible owner.
findings.resources: Two staff days from governance and operations; no new software assumed.
findings.decision: VP Engineering must approve, condition or reject continued use and fund workflow correction.
findings.closureCriteria: Authorized decision includes conditions, review date and expiry; workflow rejects unauthorized signers; independent T5 retest passes.
findings.disposition: System-specific finding; affected systems are linked.

findings.title: Monitoring reviewer not assigned for the document assistant
findings.condition: S-02 monitoring plan MON-S02 contains metrics and thresholds but no assigned reviewer or evidence of the scheduled review.
findings.criteria: Deployed systems have monitoring plans with metrics, thresholds and named reviewers.
findings.cause: The monitoring handoff checklist did not require acceptance by a named reviewer.
findings.effect: Incorrect or outdated engineering guidance could persist without timely review.
findings.recommendation: Assign a monitoring reviewer and deputy, complete and record the first review, and add reviewer acceptance to the handoff checklist.
findings.severityWhy: A meaningful operating weakness affects the moderate-tier document assistant; source verification and human review reduce current exposure.
findings.safeguards: Users verify cited source procedures before acting; the applications lead reviews reported issues daily pending formal assignment.
findings.dependencies: None beyond the named decision and responsible owner.
findings.resources: One staff day to establish ownership and review records; one hour weekly thereafter.
findings.decision: Sponsor confirms reviewer capacity and accepts the weekly review commitment.
findings.closureCriteria: Reviewer and deputy are named and acknowledge responsibility; first review is recorded; independent T10 retest passes.
findings.disposition: System-specific finding; affected systems are linked.

summary:
TRAINING ONLY. Coastal Engineering Services Engineering Operations is a fictional organization. The assessment covers a census of three operating AI systems. Overall capability is level 3 Defined against a target of level 4 Managed. Seven domains are level 3; Risk Appetite and Decision Criteria is level 2 because a high-impact residual risk acceptance was signed outside delegated authority.

Thirty-one practices meet the assessed expectations and two have verified operating gaps. Leadership should first resolve the S-01 acceptance decision and maintain independent human scheduling authorization. It should also assign S-02 monitoring responsibility and resource recurring review. The findings have accountable owners, November 27 due dates and observable closure criteria.

The results demonstrate the method only. Evidence is synthetic and does not establish assurance for real systems. No domain has the domain-wide measurement evidence needed for level 4.

T3.criteria: Required risk assessment was completed before first deployment; subsequent reassessment records are current.
T3.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T4.criteria: Pre-deployment go/no-go record was signed by the delegated decision authority.
T4.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T5.criteria: Residual risk acceptance identifies the correct delegated authority, conditions, expiry and review date.
T5.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T6.criteria: Documented human roles include the required override/stop responsibilities and evidence of their use or exercise.
T6.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T7.criteria: System impact assessment is complete and communicated to the required roles.
T7.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T8.criteria: Third-party due diligence was completed before acquisition and required contractual protections are recorded.
T8.applicability: Applies to S-01 and S-02, which use third-party AI. S-03 is in-house with no third-party AI component and is excluded with explanation.

T9.criteria: Defined evaluation criteria were tested with independence appropriate to tier.
T9.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T10.criteria: Monitoring plan has metrics, thresholds, named reviewer and records of required review.
T10.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T11.criteria: Material changes triggered reassessment and the current tier-based review is on schedule.
T11.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T12.criteria: Users can report problems and appeal relevant outcomes; channel records show tracking.
T12.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T13.criteria: Required role-based training is complete for the system team.
T13.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.

T14.criteria: Fallback, safe disengagement and retirement arrangements are documented and exercised as required.
T14.applicability: Applies to all three in-operation systems; evaluate required records and observations for each system.
